causes.reason: A Schema Object's `type` is one open field: the listed type names plus any other string (the validator rejects an unknown one), and from 3.1 also an array of them. The previous types split each Schema Object into an array variant (`type: 'array'` with a required `items`) and a non-array variant (`type` closed to the other names), so `schema.type === 'array'` narrowed `items` to required; with one variant, an open `type` and an optional `items`, that check no longer narrows.

From 3.1 a schema may be a boolean (`true` accepts anything, `false` nothing), as JSON Schema 2020-12 allows wherever a subschema goes: `items`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, and the `schema` of a Parameter, Header or Media Type Object. The previous 3.1 types accepted only Schema and Reference Objects there.

The previous 3.1 types reused the 3.0 Parameter and Header Objects, so a schema inside a 3.1 parameter or header (or its `content`) was a 3.0 Schema Object, with boolean `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum` and a `nullable` flag. The 3.1 and 3.2 Schema Object follows JSON Schema 2020-12: numeric `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum` (also accepting the 3.0 boolean form, which migrated documents carry) and no `nullable` (a 3.1 schema writes `type: [..., 'null']`).

The 3.1 and 3.2 Header Object has no `allowEmptyValue` or `allowReserved`: the official 3.1 and 3.2 schemas define neither (the 3.0 Header Object did). The previous types reused the 3.0 Header Object for 3.1.

Every map in a specification object (paths, responses, callbacks, security requirements, components, `content`, ...) is `SpecMap<T>` = `Record<string, T | undefined>`: a lookup can miss, and a document imported as a JSON module needs `undefined` values where sibling maps have different keys (see src/spec/types/common.ts). The previous types declared map values as always present.

The previous Document types declared two fields of one server framework, `x-express-openapi-additional-middleware` and `x-express-openapi-validation-strict`. They are not part of the OpenAPI specification; extension fields are read through `WithExtensions`.

The Security Scheme Object is one object with an open `type` ('apiKey' | 'http' | 'oauth2' | 'openIdConnect' | any string): only `type` is required, and the fields each type needs (`scheme` for http, `name` and `in` for apiKey, ...) are optional, checked by the validator. The previous types were a union with one variant per `type`, each requiring its own fields.

From 3.1 a document needs one of `paths`, `components` and `webhooks`, so each is optional in the type and the validator checks that one is present. The previous 3.1 Document type was a union of three variants, each requiring one of them, and is compared here with the variant requiring `paths`.

From 3.1 an operation's `responses` is optional (the 3.0 schema required it). The previous 3.1 Path Item extended the 3.0 one, so each of its operations was the intersection of the 3.0 and 3.1 Operation Objects: `responses` stayed required, and its schema and response values were intersections such as Reference Object & Schema Object or Response Object & Reference Object, which require `$ref`. Our Schema Object's `$ref` is optional and our Response Object has none.
3.2 makes a Response Object's `description` optional; the 3.0 and 3.1 schemas require it.
A server variable's `enum` is `string[]`; the previous 3.1 type was a non-empty tuple (`[string, ...string[]]`). The official schema's `minItems: 1` is left to the validator.

Public inputs that take a spec value accept `object` (and `toJsonSchema` a boolean schema too), as the factories do, so a document typed with the caller's own interfaces is accepted. The previous parameter types were the old OpenAPI unions; anything callers passed is still accepted.

These options hand the callbacks `filterFn` and `toolNameGenerator` an operation of this package's OpenAPI types, which differ from the previous ones as the other causes describe. A callback typed against a third party's OpenAPI types must be retyped to `OperationWithContext` / `OperationObject` from this package.

OpenAPI 3.2 adds the `query` operation and `additionalOperations`, whose methods are arbitrary HTTP method tokens, so a method is no longer one of eight literals: `HTTPMethod` is the nine standard methods (`get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `options`, `trace`, `query`) plus any string. A `switch` over a method needs a `default` branch, a `Record<HTTPMethod, T>` literal needs a `query` key, and a callback typed with a narrower method (such as a naming function taking only the standard methods) is rejected; `isStandardMethod` tells a standard method from another but returns a boolean, not a type guard, so narrow with `getOperation`, whose `fixed` entry types the method as a `StandardMethod`.

`OpenAPIVersion` is any `3.0.x`, `3.1.x` or `3.2.x` string instead of five literals (`'3.0.0'` to `'3.0.3'` and `'3.1.0'`), because OpenAPI patch versions such as `3.0.4` and `3.1.2` exist, tooling should ignore the patch, and 3.2 is supported: a value of the type is no longer assignable to a union of those literals, and a `switch` over it is no longer exhaustive; `detectSpecVersion(...).family` (`'2.0' | '3.0' | '3.1' | '3.2'`, or `undefined` when the document cannot be processed) is the closed value to switch on.

`OpenAPIToolGenerator` gains two public methods, `getDiagnostics()` (what the generator noticed without failing: each finding has a `severity`, a `code`, a `message` and a JSON Pointer `path`) and `getSpecVersion()` (the declared version, as `detectSpecVersion` reports it); callers of the class are unaffected, and only a hand-written stand-in typed as the class's public members needs to add them.

`ResponseBuilder` gains the public method `buildStream(responses?)`, which returns the streamed response of an operation (a `ResponseStreamInfo` built from an OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema`) or `undefined`; code that calls or extends the class is unaffected, and only a hand-written stand-in typed as the class's public members needs to add it.
